glossary.definition: The context window is the amount of text an AI model can "see" and consider at once, including your prompt, any documents you've shared, and the conversation history so far. It's like a person's short-term memory during a conversation: once you're past a certain point, earlier details start slipping away, and once a conversation exceeds the context window, the model genuinely stops being able to "remember" the earliest parts of it.

items.title: At SC26, Nvidia debuts new Rubin HPC chip, scientific research libraries
items.summary: Nvidia Corp. today introduced a set of offerings designed to speed up scientific research across a range of fields. The lineup is headlined by Rubin HPC, an upcoming graphics card with significantly more cores than the company’s current flagship chip. It’s joined by more than a half-dozen software tools geared toward scientists and engineers. The technologies made their debut at the SC26 high-performance and supercomputing conference in Chicago.

items.title: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
items.summary: Three months since introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corba has raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA. Three months after introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corma has raised a $125 million Series A round at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, the company said. Corma offers AI models and agents trained for cybersecurity defense. It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue.

items.title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
items.summary: Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO. At the center of this theory is the reporting from The New York Times that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, one of multiple women Huang is accused of having an affair with, is a Chinese spy. David Sacks, Tim Sweeney, and other big names in tech are raising questions about the circumstances surrounding Huang’s resignation.

items.title: All the questions Nvidia should answer on Tuesday — but probably won’t
items.summary: Nvidia interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress is about to have one of the biggest days of her career on Tuesday when the company reports its third-quarter results. Given the turmoil Nvidia is in, there are a number of questions that Nvidia should answer. For the first time, Kress will be running through the numbers and sharing guidance without Nvidia’s charismatic but now-disgraced founder Jensen Huang. Huang was forced to resign last week after he admitted to having an affair with an exec of a customer, Alice Huang, a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, and he was accused of having two more affairs with Nvidia employees.

items.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
items.summary: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday , Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters . OpenAI lost control of its AI agents more than 80 times during testing, California’s AG claims. ” It alleges that OpenAI recently told the attorney general’s office that it “lost control” of its AI agents more than 80 times during testing.

items.title: Google warns that fully automated cyberattacks have arrived and will get worse fast
items.summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group has for the first time caught attackers finding and exploiting security vulnerabilities with no human involvement at all. An AI framework called "exploit_agent," found on an exposed server, automatically compared code before and after patches, built exploits, and ran them on its own. Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) says it has observed attackers fully automating vulnerability discovery and exploitation for the first time, with no human in the loop. GTIG found an exposed server running an AI framework called "exploit_agent" that connects to multiple language models, according to the GTIG AI Threat Tracker .

items.title: The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back
items.summary: On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world. These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry’s critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech).

items.title: Jensen Huang Is Gone. Now What?
items.summary: After a shocking downfall, Nvidia’s CEO is out of a job. WIRED’s Lauren Goode explains what that means for the world’s most critical chip company, the AI industry, and Jensen Huang himself. I don’t go into any given week at WIRED assuming I’ll be thinking much about extramarital affairs. But last week, they were the only thing on my mind.

items.title: Alibaba Launches Qwen4-Max AI Model With Focus on Security
items.summary: Alibaba has introduced Qwen4-Max, its latest flagship artificial intelligence (AI) model. Built on a new architecture with 2.4 trillion parameters and a 1-million-token context window, the model is designed for complex professional and scientific tasks. “It can take on a wide range of creative and professional work,” Alibaba said, citing applications in 3D modelling, game development, precision manufacturing, finance, law, healthcare, and scientific discovery. Qwen4-Max succeeds Qwen3.8-Max, which Alibaba launched in August.

items.title: Alibaba touts 62% lower task costs with Qwen4-Max, adds cyber safeguards
items.summary: Alibaba has released Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter flagship model, claiming it reduces the average cost of completing professional tasks by 62% compared with its predecessor while introducing additional safeguards against offensive cybersecurity capabilities and other high-risk uses. “According to Work360 — a proprietary benchmark evaluating performance on challenging industry tasks across 721 specialized fields — Qwen4-Max outperforms its predecessor, Qwen3.8-Max, overall while using 35% fewer tokens at High effort reasoning mode and reducing the average cost per task by around 60%,” Alibaba said in a blog post. The Qwen team’s announcement puts the average task cost at $1.67 for Qwen4-Max, compared with $4.43 for Qwen3.8-Max, representing a 62% reduction. The model keeps the 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts backbone of its predecessor, Qwen3.8-Max, but activates about 71 billion parameters per token instead of about 95 billion, the company said.

items.title: Delhi's Bharat Semi Raises $24 Mn to Develop AI Image Sensors
items.summary: Delhi-based semiconductor startup Bharat Semi has raised $24 million (₹215 crore) in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors. The funding will support product development and expansion as the company targets customers in the US and other global markets. The all-equity funding round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures. Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels, and individual investors also participated.

items.title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess
items.summary: AI competitors are catching up to Nvidia—and poised to take advantage of the chaos. Nvidia played a key role enabling the AI gold rush thanks in large part to its recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang . Huang was a master of foreseeing technological changes , investing in chips to train AI earlier than most. But just as he’s leaving , the company has a growing list of competitors with a range of new, advanced technology breathing down its neck.
